question: Which public URL does the file app/(marketing)/pricing/page.tsx resolve to?
options: It is ignored because parentheses mark private folders
explanation: Folders wrapped in parentheses like (marketing) are Route Groups. Next.js uses them to organize files and share layouts, and strips them completely from the public URL.

question: What happens if a developer places a file at app/dashboard/_widgets/MetricsChart.tsx (or even app/dashboard/_widgets/page.tsx)?
options: Any folder prefixed with an underscore is opted out of routing and never creates a public URL
Next.js renders it only for authenticated admin users
It resolves to /dashboard/widgets with the underscore stripped
It acts as a global fallback route for 404 errors
explanation: Prefixing a folder with an underscore (_widgets) marks it as a private folder. The App Router excludes private folders and their descendants from URL routing.

question: Given app/docs/[...slug]/page.tsx (with no app/docs/page.tsx), which URL does NOT match?
explanation: A single-bracket catch-all segment ([...slug]) requires at least one segment after /docs. To match /docs itself without a separate page.tsx, you must use an optional catch-all [[...slug]].

question: If both app/blog/featured/page.tsx and app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx exist, which component renders for /blog/featured?
options: Next.js throws a duplicate route build error
Whichever file was modified most recently
app/blog/featured/page.tsx because static segments have higher precedence than dynamic segments
explanation: App Router route resolution prioritizes static segments over dynamic [param] segments, which in turn take precedence over catch-all [...param] and optional catch-all [[...param]] routes.
